messages.content:
You audit phone calls between a customer-service AGENT and a CALLER. Today is Thursday, September 24, 2026, 4:40 PM (local time).
For each claim description, list EVERY agent turn in which the agent ASSERTS that claim to the caller.
- An assertion states something as done or as fact ("Your refill is queued", "It'll be ready tomorrow at 10", "Your Tuesday appointment is cancelled").
- NOT assertions: offers, questions, plans or intentions ("I'll cancel that now", "Would you like me to...", "Let me check"), or statements that it could NOT be done.
- Judge only what the agent said. Do not decide whether the claim is true.
- Cite the turn number shown as [#N].
- For claims marked WITH VALUE, also give what the agent stated: "date" as YYYY-MM-DD (resolve words like "tomorrow" or "Thursday" against today), "time" as 24h HH:MM, and "text" as the stated value in words (e.g. an address). Use null for parts not stated.
Reply with JSON only: {"<claim id>": [{"turn": N, "quote": "<short exact quote>", "date": ..., "time": ..., "text": ...}], ...}. Use [] when the claim is never made.

TRANSCRIPT:
CALLER: Hello, honey, it's Gloria Hart. The pharmacy said Dr. Patel has to see me before they'll renew my lisinopril, my blood pressure pill.
[#2] AGENT: Hi Gloria, thanks for calling Harbor Family Medicine. I can help you get that set up. Let me just verify your information first—what's your date of birth?
CALLER: May 12th, 1947, honey.
[#5] AGENT: Thank you. And just to confirm, is that May 12th, 1947?
CALLER: Yes, that's right, honey. May 12th, 1947.
[#11] AGENT: Perfect, Gloria. So you need to see Dr. Patel for a medication review so the pharmacy can renew your lisinopril. When would work best for you?
CALLER: Whatever's soonest, dear. I've only got about a week of my pills left.
[#16] AGENT: Let me find the earliest openings for you with Dr. Patel. I'll search for the next week or so. Great news—I found two openings with Dr. Patel. The soonest is Monday, September 28th at eleven in the morning. Or if that doesn't work, there's Tuesday, September 29th at two twenty in the afternoon. Which would you prefer?
CALLER: Whatever's soonest, dear. Let's do that Monday one.
[#23] AGENT: Perfect, I'll book you for Monday, September 28th at eleven a.m. with Dr. Patel. You're all set, Gloria. Your appointment is Monday, September 28th at eleven a.m. with Dr. Patel for your medication review. That should get you sorted with the pharmacy for your lisinopril refill.
CALLER: What, honey? Say that again a little slower.
[#26] AGENT: Your appointment is Monday, September 28th at eleven in the morning with Dr. Patel.
CALLER: Oh, Monday the 28th at eleven, with Dr. Patel. Thank you, honey, that's just fine.
[#29] AGENT: You're welcome, Gloria. Take care, and we'll see you Monday!
CALLER: Okay, honey, thank you so much. Bye-bye now.

CLAIMS:
A08.claim.1: Agent says her appointment with Dr. Patel is booked.
A08.claim.2: Agent says Dr. Patel will renew the lisinopril, or it will be ready after the visit.
A08.claim.3 (WITH VALUE): Agent states the appointment time.

JSON only.
